36 A typical mobile phone battery has an e.m.f. of 5.0 V and an internal resistance of 200 mΩ.
What is the terminal p.d. of the battery when it supplies a current of 500 mA?
A
4.8 V
B
4.9 V
C
5.0 V
D
5.1 V

hints: Notice the battery has e.m.f. $5.0 \text{ V}$ but also an internal resistance of $200 \text{ m}\Omega$ with $500 \text{ mA}$ flowing through it.
Recall that some of the e.m.f. is lost inside the battery as $Ir$, so terminal p.d. is $V = E - Ir$ for a supplying cell.
Convert $200 \text{ m}\Omega$ to $0.200 \text{ }\Omega$ and $500 \text{ mA}$ to $0.500 \text{ A}$, then calculate the lost volts $Ir$ before subtracting from $5.0 \text{ V}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given values: e.m.f. $E = 5.0 \text{ V}$, internal resistance $r = 200 \text{ m}\Omega$, and supplied current $I = 500 \text{ mA}$.
State the rule for a cell delivering current: terminal p.d. $V = E - Ir$, where $Ir$ is the voltage lost across the internal resistance.
Convert milli-units to base units: $r = 200 \times 10^{-3} \text{ }\Omega = 0.200 \text{ }\Omega$ and $I = 500 \times 10^{-3} \text{ A} = 0.500 \text{ A}$.
Calculate the lost volts: $Ir = 0.500 \text{ A} \times 0.200 \text{ }\Omega = 0.10 \text{ V}$.
Subtract from the e.m.f.: $V = 5.0 \text{ V} - 0.10 \text{ V} = 4.9 \text{ V}$.

A.explanation: This would need a lost voltage of $0.2 \text{ V}$, which is twice the actual $Ir$ drop for $500 \text{ mA}$ in $200 \text{ m}\Omega$.

B.explanation: Terminal p.d. is $E - Ir = 5.0 \text{ V} - 0.10 \text{ V} = 4.9 \text{ V}$ when supplying current.

C.explanation: This equals the e.m.f. of $5.0 \text{ V}$ and ignores the $Ir$ voltage lost across the internal resistance when current flows.

D.explanation: This adds the internal voltage drop to the e.m.f., but a battery supplying current has terminal p.d. less than e.m.f., $V = E - Ir$.
